A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VLSA research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original survival-prediction experiments on five TCGA datasets, including baseline comparisons, ablations, few-shot evaluation, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds comparator results, risk-group survival analysis, and time-discretization controls.

M1.justification: The prior-guided aggregation, ordinal prompt interpolation, incidence prediction, MLE-plus-EMD objective, and Shapley interpretation remain unchanged. Replacing 'cross-attention' with 'similarity matching and weighted averaging' clarifies the unchanged Equation (2). Both appendices specify the same four base prompts despite different illustrative examples in Section 3.2.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same five TCGA cohorts—BLCA, BRCA, GBMLGG, LUAD, and UCEC—with 2,831 patients and 3,530 WSIs, including full-shot and few-shot settings. The added multimodal comparisons substitute existing textual priors for gene inputs; they introduce no genomic dataset or new task coverage.

E2.justification: v4 adds R2T-MIL and ABMILPrompt to the main, few-shot, and efficiency comparisons, plus MI-FewShot to Table 4. New Table 9 evaluates MCAT, MMPTrans., MMPOT, and MOTCat with textual priors replacing gene inputs. These additions substantially broaden the comparator set while retaining earlier baselines.

E3.justification: Existing cross-validation, few-shot sampling, and training settings are retained. Added protocols include cohort-median risk grouping for Kaplan–Meier analysis, four quantile bins for incidence-based VLSA, and square-root-of-event-count bins for Patch-GCN (Appendices D.1 and D.6). These are focused additional evaluations, not revisions to the original experiments.

E4.justification: v4 adds risk-stratification analysis and extends discretization sensitivity testing with the four-quantile-bin setting and a Patch-GCN bin-count control. The ordinal ablation without prognostic priors already appeared in v1 Table 8 and is merged into v4 Table 3. Existing component ablations, hazard/PLIP analyses, and visual case studies are retained.

E5.justification: v4 adds log-rank significance tests and p-values for the risk groups in Figure 5. Both versions retain five-fold averages, tabulated plus/minus values, and five repeated few-shot runs summarized by medians. No increase in repeated-run counts is reported.

E6.justification: New comparator and control results substantially expand the reported evidence. v4 Table 9 reports average CI 0.6669 for MOTCat versus 0.6954 for VLSA; Tables 10–11 add CI 0.6844 for four-quantile-bin VLSA and 0.6625 for Patch-GCN with more bins. Kaplan–Meier results are also added. Matched earlier results remain unchanged, including VLSA's main average CI of 0.6954.

T1.justification: v4 corrects the concluding assertion of the geometric counterexample: v1 Appendix C says the incidence function is 'ordinal everywhere' immediately after describing an exception, whereas v4 Appendix B explicitly states that non-ordinal predictions can occur despite ordinal prompts. The equations, assumptions, and underlying counterexample otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: the first VL-based WSI survival framework, language-guided aggregation, ordinal inductive biases, Shapley interpretation, and performance/data-efficiency advantages. Added experiments support these existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 adds a mechanism hypothesis: stronger prior-guided visual features reduce the additional CI benefit of ordinal prompts, while ordinal incidence constraints primarily improve MAE. Section 3.1 explicitly distinguishes textual guidance from multimodal feature fusion. The earlier limitations are largely relocated intact, with an added future direction involving stronger WSI representation methods.

D1.justification: v4 newly specifies 448-by-448 patches at 20× magnification, two RTX 3090 GPUs with 24 GB memory, and further baseline/discretization implementation details. Existing hyperparameters and training settings are retained. The code URL was already supplied in v1 Appendix D.4; its appearance in v4's abstract is not a new resource release.

R1.justification: v4 adds focused literature coverage for multimodal survival models, recent MIL methods, few-shot prediction, and discretization conventions. It explicitly positions prior-guided aggregation against multimodal fusion. The overall research positioning, first-VLSA novelty claim, and organization of Section 2 remain stable.

P1.justification: v4 makes targeted language and terminology edits and expands several explanations. Computation efficiency and limitations move into the appendices, which gain a contents page and numbered supplementary subsections. The principal narrative and much of the wording remain intact.

P2.justification: The results displays are substantially reorganized: v1 Tables 3 and 8 become one grouped Table 3; main, few-shot, and efficiency tables gain comparator rows; and v4 adds Kaplan–Meier Figure 5 and comparison Tables 9 and 11. The efficiency table is relocated, and diagram labels and captions are revised. Most earlier plots are retained.

improvement.justification: Added fixed-prompt, recent MIL, and adapted multimodal comparators, together with Patch-GCN bin-count controls, strengthen the comparative evidence. New preprocessing and hardware details also help reproduction. The gains extend an already extensive v1 evaluation. They are tempered by different cutoff strategies in the four-bin comparison and an inconsistency in new Figure 5: its caption calls blue 'low-risk' although the blue curves show lower survival.
